GIBRALTAR PORT AUTHORITY LNTM 037/2026
LOCAL NOTICE TO MARINERS 2026 LNTM 036
2026 LNTM 037 - Demolition of Extension Jetty

To: All Mariners, Owners, Agents and Charterers;

The Southern section of the Extension Jetty will shortly be demolished and removed from the area
of the Inner Harbour.

Works will start as from today (24/08/2026) and be conducted by the barge “K9128” which will be
moored alongside the Jetty.
The barge will be moored alongside the Extension jetty during the works and will deploy a silt screen
around itself and the Extension Jetty. In addition, there will be and anchor chain deployed to the
South of the Jetty that will be marked by a Light Buoy. There will be a strict 30m Exclusion Zone to
the East and West of the Jetty and 100m to the South.

All maritime users are to keep away from this area at all times. Maritime users are also to keep to
the South of the marker buoy to avoid the barge’s anchor chain.

Mariners are to transit the area with extreme caution if absolutely necessary.

GIBRALTAR PORT AUTHORITY LNTM 008/2026
2026 LNTM 008 - CETACEAN PROTOCOL

LOCAL NOTICE TO MARINERS NO 008 OF 2026 CETACEAN PROTOCOL

To: All Mariners, Owners, Agents and Charterers;

You are reminded that, all Cetaceans (Whales and Dolphins) and marine reptiles
(Turtles) are protected by law in British Gibraltar Territorial Waters under the
Nature Protection Act 1991.

The Mobile Cetacean Conservation Area is defined as an imaginary cylinder of
sea and air space with a 500m radius centred on the cetacean or group of
cetaceans, with a height of 500m into the air and a depth of 60m under the sea.
The Marine Protection Regulations Cetacean Protocol shall apply within this
space. (See attached protocol).

All vessels must maintain a sharp lookout and reduce speed to 4 knots if they
sight any animals.

All vessels are to keep a minimum distance of 60 meters from any animal or group
of animals.

All vessels must comply with the Nature Protection Act 1991 and the Marine
Protection Regulations Cetacean Protocol in its entirety. (See attached protocol).

w.t:
GIBRALTAR PORT AUTHORITY LNTM 006/2026
2026 LNTM 006 - USE OF MOBILE TELEPHONE REPEATER
EQUIPMENT IN GIBRALTAR WATERS

To: All Mariners, Owners, Agents and Charterers;

All Mariners, Owners, Agents and Charterers are reminded that any mobile telephone LTE
(2G/3G/4G/5G) (GSM/UMTS/LTE) repeaters and/or base stations including pico and nano
cells, fitted on vessels, must be switched off at all times whilst in Gibraltar Territorial Waters
and remain switched off until they leave the jurisdiction.

These devices cause serious interference to authorised Gibraltar mobile telephone networks
and any vessel found operating them whilst in Territorial Waters will be subject to investigation
by the Gibraltar Regulatory Authority (GRA).

Agents and Marinas must ensure that all vessels calling at Gibraltar are advised of these
regulations immediately on their arrival.

For further information contact the Gibraltar Port Authority or the Gibraltar Regulatory Authority
(www.gra.gi / radio@gra.gi ).
